[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. If the bidding actuarial rate for a crop is lower than the prescribed ceiling (for example, 1.2% for a Kharif food grain), the farmer pays the lower actuarial rate (1.2%), not 2.0%.

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

Under the 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines, Central Government premium subsidy is subject to explicit actuarial premium rate ceilings and regional sharing ratios detailed in Table 2:

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q1: What is the premium rate payable by farmers under PMFBY? Answer: Under PMFBY, farmers pay a uniform maximum premium of 2.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for all Kharif food grain and oilseed crops; 1.5% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for all Rabi food grain and oilseed crops; and 5.0% of Sum Insured (or Actuarial rate, whichever is less) for Annual Commercial and Annual Horticultural crops.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

rankings.text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. rankings.text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (PMFBY) ? REVAMPED OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES (2023 EDITION)] Note on Document Pagination: This cover sheet is Physical PDF Page 1 (unnumbered). The Table of Contents is Physical PDF Page 2 (Printed Page i). Substantive operational clauses begin on Physical PDF Page 3 (Printed Page 1).

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Central and State Government Premium Subsidy Sharing and Actuarial Rate Ceilings] The difference between the Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) and the maximum insurance charges payable by farmers is treated as the Normal Premium Subsidy. Under the 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines, Central Government premium subsidy is subject to explicit actuarial premium rate ceilings and regional sharing ratios detailed in Table 2:

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

rankings.text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

rankings.text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Table: Table 4: Operational Cut-Off Dates, Penal Interest, and Administrative Expense Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Operational Rule: Delayed Claim Settlement / Delayed Subsidy Penal Interest | Season / Stakeholder: Insurance Companies and State Governments | Numerical Value: 12.0% | Unit / Basis: % per annum (simple interest on delayed claim/subsidy amount) | Qualification / Condition: Insurance companies must pay 12.0% per annum interest to farmers for claim delays beyond prescribed cut-off (21 days after receipt of yield data/subsidy); States pay 12.0% interest for subsidy delays

[Table: Table 3: Indemnity Levels, Risk Coverage Triggers, Payout Caps, and Reporting Timelines (2023 Guidelines)] Provision / Risk Component: Mid-Season Adversity Immediate Relief | Applicable Crop / Scope: Notified crops experiencing severe mid-season calamity | Numerical Value / Limit: 25.0% | Unit / Basis: % of likely claims | Mandatory Qualification / Trigger Condition: Advance on-account payment up to 25.0% of likely claims when expected yield during the season falls below 50.0% of normal/threshold yield

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (PMFBY) ? REVAMPED OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES (2023 EDITION)] Note on Document Pagination: This cover sheet is Physical PDF Page 1 (unnumbered). The Table of Contents is Physical PDF Page 2 (Printed Page i). Substantive operational clauses begin on Physical PDF Page 3 (Printed Page 1).

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Central and State Government Premium Subsidy Sharing and Actuarial Rate Ceilings] The difference between the Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) and the maximum insurance charges payable by farmers is treated as the Normal Premium Subsidy. Under the 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines, Central Government premium subsidy is subject to explicit actuarial premium rate ceilings and regional sharing ratios detailed in Table 2:

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

rankings.text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

rankings.text: [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Table: Table 4: Operational Cut-Off Dates, Penal Interest, and Administrative Expense Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Operational Rule: Delayed Claim Settlement / Delayed Subsidy Penal Interest | Season / Stakeholder: Insurance Companies and State Governments | Numerical Value: 12.0% | Unit / Basis: % per annum (simple interest on delayed claim/subsidy amount) | Qualification / Condition: Insurance companies must pay 12.0% per annum interest to farmers for claim delays beyond prescribed cut-off (21 days after receipt of yield data/subsidy); States pay 12.0% interest for subsidy delays

[Table: Table 3: Indemnity Levels, Risk Coverage Triggers, Payout Caps, and Reporting Timelines (2023 Guidelines)] Provision / Risk Component: Mid-Season Adversity Immediate Relief | Applicable Crop / Scope: Notified crops experiencing severe mid-season calamity | Numerical Value / Limit: 25.0% | Unit / Basis: % of likely claims | Mandatory Qualification / Trigger Condition: Advance on-account payment up to 25.0% of likely claims when expected yield during the season falls below 50.0% of normal/threshold yield

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. [Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA (PMFBY) ? REVAMPED OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES (2023 EDITION)] Note on Document Pagination: This cover sheet is Physical PDF Page 1 (unnumbered). The Table of Contents is Physical PDF Page 2 (Printed Page i). Substantive operational clauses begin on Physical PDF Page 3 (Printed Page 1).

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Central and State Government Premium Subsidy Sharing and Actuarial Rate Ceilings] The difference between the Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) and the maximum insurance charges payable by farmers is treated as the Normal Premium Subsidy. Under the 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines, Central Government premium subsidy is subject to explicit actuarial premium rate ceilings and regional sharing ratios detailed in Table 2:

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

rankings.text: [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Table: Table 1 (2016 Historical Edition): Farmer Premium Rates and Uncapped Subsidy Sharing (2016-2020)] Provision: Historical Loanee Farmer Enrolment | Season / Scope: Loanee farmers with KCC / SAO crop loans | 2016 Historical Value: 100.0% mandatory (compulsory) | Unit / Basis: % of loanee farmers in notified area | Historical Qualification (Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31): Compulsory for loanee farmers under 2016 guidelines; replaced by 100% voluntary participation from Kharif 2020 onwards

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Table: Table 1 (2016 Historical Edition): Farmer Premium Rates and Uncapped Subsidy Sharing (2016-2020)] Provision: Historical Central Premium Subsidy Sharing (All States including NER) | Season / Scope: All States including North Eastern States (2016-2020) | 2016 Historical Value: 50:50 (50.0% Central share, 50.0% State share) | Unit / Basis: Balance Normal Premium Subsidy | Historical Qualification (Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31): Under the 2016 guidelines prior to the 2020 revamp, Central and State Governments shared the balance subsidy 50:50 across all States with NO 30%/25% actuarial rate ceiling (100% uncapped actuarial subsidy)

[Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Wild Animal Attack Add-on Cover: Losses caused by wild animal attacks were historically excluded from basic cover. States have been permitted to notify wild animal attack as an add-on cover based on individual assessment, implemented 100.0% at the cost of the respective State Government (0.0% Central Government subsidy liability for wild animal add-on cover). A technical committee submitted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for wild animal attack loss assessment and localized inundation for paddy crops.

REVAMPED OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES (2023 EDITION)] Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Document Version: 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines (applicable from Kharif 2020 revamp as updated in 2023).

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[Table: Table 4: Operational Cut-Off Dates, Penal Interest, and Administrative Expense Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Operational Rule: Claim Settlement Timeline after Yield Data & Subsidy Receipt | Season / Stakeholder: Implementing Insurance Companies | Numerical Value: 21 days | Unit / Basis: Days from receipt of yield data and premium subsidy | Qualification / Condition: Claims must be settled within 21 days (3 weeks) after receipt of both final yield data and Central/State subsidy share

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Table: Table 1 (2016 Historical Edition): Farmer Premium Rates and Uncapped Subsidy Sharing (2016-2020)] Provision: Historical Central Premium Subsidy Sharing (All States including NER) | Season / Scope: All States including North Eastern States (2016-2020) | 2016 Historical Value: 50:50 (50.0% Central share, 50.0% State share) | Unit / Basis: Balance Normal Premium Subsidy | Historical Qualification (Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31): Under the 2016 guidelines prior to the 2020 revamp, Central and State Governments shared the balance subsidy 50:50 across all States with NO 30%/25% actuarial rate ceiling (100% uncapped actuarial subsidy)

[Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Wild Animal Attack Add-on Cover: Losses caused by wild animal attacks were historically excluded from basic cover. States have been permitted to notify wild animal attack as an add-on cover based on individual assessment, implemented 100.0% at the cost of the respective State Government (0.0% Central Government subsidy liability for wild animal add-on cover). A technical committee submitted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for wild animal attack loss assessment and localized inundation for paddy crops.

However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Table: Table 2: Premium Subsidy Sharing Pattern and Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Rule Parameter: Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceiling (Unirrigated) | Applicable Category / Geography: Unirrigated (Rainfed) areas/crops (districts with less than 50% irrigated area) | Prescribed Numerical Value / Ratio: 30.0% | Basis / Denominator: Actuarial Premium Rate (% of Sum Insured) | Qualification and Operational Condition: Central Government subsidy is capped for actuarial premium rates up to 30.0%; subsidy above 30.0% is borne by the State/UT

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Operational Sampling and Outreach Benchmarks: For estimation of crop yield at the Gram Panchayat (Insurance Unit) level, a minimum of 4 Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) are mandatory for major crops, and 8 CCEs are required at the Mandal/Taluka level. Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. (Note: The 30% women outreach target, 2.0 hectares small-farmer landholding threshold, and 5% weekly block camp coverage are administrative outreach targets, NOT farmer insurance premium rates.)

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana ? Operational Guidelines (2016 Original Edition, Effective 2016-04-01 to 2020-03-31)] Historical Compulsory Enrolment Rule (2016-2020): Under the 2016 Operational Guidelines (effective from Kharif 2016, 2016-04-01 until superseded by the Revamped Guidelines on 2020-03-31), PMFBY enrolment was 100% compulsory (mandatory) for all loanee farmers availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) credit / Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans for notified crops, and voluntary only for non-loanee farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Criteria for Assessing Losses under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (Published 12 DEC 2025)] Wild Animal Attack Add-on Cover: Losses caused by wild animal attacks were historically excluded from basic cover. States have been permitted to notify wild animal attack as an add-on cover based on individual assessment, implemented 100.0% at the cost of the respective State Government (0.0% Central Government subsidy liability for wild animal add-on cover). A technical committee submitted Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for wild animal attack loss assessment and localized inundation for paddy crops.

REVAMPED OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES (2023 EDITION)] Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. Document Version: 2023 Revamped Operational Guidelines (applicable from Kharif 2020 revamp as updated in 2023).

[Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged by the implementing insurance company as determined by competitive bidding. However, the maximum insurance charges (premium) payable by the farmer under PMFBY (2023 Operational Guidelines) are strictly capped according to season and crop category as specified in Table 1 below:

[Table: Table 4: Operational Cut-Off Dates, Penal Interest, and Administrative Expense Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Operational Rule: Claim Settlement Timeline after Yield Data & Subsidy Receipt | Season / Stakeholder: Implementing Insurance Companies | Numerical Value: 21 days | Unit / Basis: Days from receipt of yield data and premium subsidy | Qualification / Condition: Claims must be settled within 21 days (3 weeks) after receipt of both final yield data and Central/State subsidy share

[Table: Table 2: Premium Subsidy Sharing Pattern and Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Rule Parameter: Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceiling (Irrigated) | Applicable Category / Geography: Irrigated areas/crops (districts with 50.0% or more irrigated area) | Prescribed Numerical Value / Ratio: 25.0% | Basis / Denominator: Actuarial Premium Rate (% of Sum Insured) | Qualification and Operational Condition: Central Government subsidy is capped for actuarial premium rates up to 25.0%; subsidy above 25.0% is borne by the State/UT

[Table: Table 2: Premium Subsidy Sharing Pattern and Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Rule Parameter: Central Subsidy Actuarial Ceiling (Unirrigated) | Applicable Category / Geography: Unirrigated (Rainfed) areas/crops (districts with less than 50% irrigated area) | Prescribed Numerical Value / Ratio: 30.0% | Basis / Denominator: Actuarial Premium Rate (% of Sum Insured) | Qualification and Operational Condition: Central Government subsidy is capped for actuarial premium rates up to 30.0%; subsidy above 30.0% is borne by the State/UT

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Sum Insured (SI) Calculation: The Sum Insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is equal to the Scale of Finance (SoF) as decided by the District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) or notified area Threshold Yield multiplied by the Minimum Support Price (MSP), reaching 100% of the full economic value without any upper reduction capping.

[Table: Table 3: Indemnity Levels, Risk Coverage Triggers, Payout Caps, and Reporting Timelines (2023 Guidelines)] Provision / Risk Component: Post-Harvest Losses Coverage Window | Applicable Crop / Scope: Crops dried in cut-and-spread / small bundled condition in field after harvesting | Numerical Value / Limit: 14 days (2 weeks) | Unit / Basis: Days from harvesting | Mandatory Qualification / Trigger Condition: Maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from actual date of harvesting against cyclone, cyclonic rain, unseasonal rain, and hailstorm

[Table: Table 3: Indemnity Levels, Risk Coverage Triggers, Payout Caps, and Reporting Timelines (2023 Guidelines)] Provision / Risk Component: Prevented / Failed Sowing On-Account Payout | Applicable Crop / Scope: Notified crops in affected Insurance Unit (IU) | Numerical Value / Limit: 25.0% | Unit / Basis: % of Sum Insured | Mandatory Qualification / Trigger Condition: Maximum payout up to 25.0% of Sum Insured, triggered only when more than 75.0% of sown area in the notified IU is prevented from sowing/germination; insurance cover terminates thereafter

[Table: Table 4: Operational Cut-Off Dates, Penal Interest, and Administrative Expense Ceilings (2023 Guidelines)] Operational Rule: Delayed Claim Settlement / Delayed Subsidy Penal Interest | Season / Stakeholder: Insurance Companies and State Governments | Numerical Value: 12.0% | Unit / Basis: % per annum (simple interest on delayed claim/subsidy amount) | Qualification / Condition: Insurance companies must pay 12.0% per annum interest to farmers for claim delays beyond prescribed cut-off (21 days after receipt of yield data/subsidy); States pay 12.0% interest for subsidy delays

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

Under the National Crop Insurance Portal outreach drive (Krishi Rakshak Helpline 14447), field agencies target at least 30% participation from women cultivators and small/marginal farmers holding less than 2.0 hectares of operational land, with digital village camps covering 5% of high-priority blocks each week. [Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. [Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. If the bidding actuarial rate for a crop is lower than the prescribed ceiling (for example, 1.2% for a Kharif food grain), the farmer pays the lower actuarial rate (1.2%), not 2.0%.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Overview] Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) provides comprehensive crop insurance coverage against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is voluntary for States as well as farmers and provides comprehensive risk insurance from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages against non-preventable natural risks.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Temporal Provenance Note: The official PMFBY FAQ web page (https://pmfby.gov.in/faq) does not carry an explicit publication date or effective-from date stamp on the document itself.

[Seasonality Discipline, Cut-Off Dates, Administrative Expenses, and Penal Interest] Standard Enrolment Cut-Off Dates: Unless specifically varied by State notification within the permissible window, the standard final cut-off date for farmer enrolment and premium debit is 31st July for the Kharif season and 31st December for the Rabi season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Scheme Objective, Coverage of Farmers, and Voluntary Participation] Under the Revamped Operational Guidelines of PMFBY (effective from Kharif 2020 and consolidated in 2023), enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is 100% voluntary for all farmers, including both loanee farmers (availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations loans / KCC) and non-loanee farmers. Loanee farmers may opt out of PMFBY by submitting a written declaration to their bank branch at least 7 days prior to the enrolment cut-off date for the respective season.

[Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) ? Official Frequently Asked Questions (Undated Portal Document)] Q4: Within how many hours must a farmer report localized crop loss or post-harvest damage? Answer: The insured farmer must intimate localized calamity losses (hailstorm, landslide, inundation, cloudburst) or post-harvest losses within 72 hours of the occurrence of the peril. Post-harvest losses are covered for a maximum period of 14 days (2 weeks) from harvesting for crops left in cut-and-spread condition in the field for drying.

rankings.text: [Maximum Insurance Charges (Premium) Payable by Farmer] Important Rule on Qualification and Basis: In all three categories of Table 1, the stated percentage (2.0% for Kharif food grain and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food grain and oilseed crops, and 5.0% for annual commercial and annual horticultural crops) is a maximum ceiling expressed as a percentage of Sum Insured (SI), subject to the mandatory qualification 'or Actuarial rate, whichever is less'. If the bidding actuarial rate for a crop is lower than the prescribed ceiling (for example, 1.2% for a Kharif food grain), the farmer pays the lower actuarial rate (1.2%), not 2.0%.
